introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
enonce_intro_markdown:
A particle $P$, of mass $2\ \mathrm{kg}$, moves in a straight horizontal line with simple harmonic motion with centre $O$. When $P$ is at a point distant $1.5$ metres from $O$, its speed is $4$ metres per second and its acceleration is $-6\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

Find
incertitudes: Question 3 : l'accélération -6 m/s^2 est supposée dirigée vers O pour un déplacement de +1,5 m depuis O (convention a = -omega^2 x), ce qui est la seule lecture cohérente avec le signe imprimé.

questions.corrige_markdown:
For simple harmonic motion with centre $O$, the acceleration is $a = -\omega^2 x$, where $x$ is the displacement from $O$. At $x = 1.5\ \mathrm{m}$, $a = -6\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$:

$$-6 = -\omega^2(1.5)\ \Rightarrow\ \omega^2 = \frac{6}{1.5} = 4\ \Rightarrow\ \omega = 2\ \mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}$$

Period:

$$T = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = \frac{2\pi}{2} = \pi\ \mathrm{s} \approx 3.14\ \mathrm{s}$$
themes: simple harmonic motion of a particle

questions.corrige_markdown:
Use $v^2 = \omega^2(A^2 - x^2)$ with $v = 4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $x = 1.5\ \mathrm{m}$ and $\omega^2 = 4$:

$$16 = 4\big(A^2 - 2.25\big)\ \Rightarrow\ A^2 - 2.25 = 4\ \Rightarrow\ A^2 = 6.25$$

$$A = 2.5\ \mathrm{m}$$
themes: simple harmonic motion of a particle

questions.corrige_markdown:
The maximum speed occurs at the centre $O$ ($x = 0$):

$$v_{\max} = \omega A = 2\times 2.5 = 5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$$

(Check with $v^2 = \omega^2(A^2 - 0) = 4\times 6.25 = 25$, so $v = 5$.)
themes: simple harmonic motion of a particle

questions.corrige_markdown:
The force is $F = ma = -m\omega^2 x$, and its magnitude is greatest at the ends of the motion, where $|x| = A$:

$$F_{\max} = m\omega^2 A = 2\times 4\times 2.5 = 20\ \mathrm{N}$$

This force is directed towards $O$.
themes: simple harmonic motion of a particle
